subject: math
title: Lines, Angles and Shapes: Rays, Parallel and Perpendicular Lines, Classifying Triangles
seo_title: Grade 4 Lines, Rays and Angles Worksheets: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines, Right Triangles (4.G.A.1-2)
standard_text: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures. Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 geometry worksheets with pictures: points, lines, line segments and rays, acute, right, obtuse and straight angles, parallel and perpendicular lines, right, acute and obtuse triangles, and sorting shapes by sides and angles. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Look at the ends and the corners: arrows go on forever, dots are endpoints, and a square corner is a right angle.
key_sub: A ray is named from its endpoint. Parallel lines never meet; perpendicular lines meet at right angles. A triangle is named by its largest angle: acute, right or obtuse.
body_html:
The building blocks of geometry

Every shape is made of a few simple figures. Look at the ends: a dot is an endpoint (the figure stops there), and an arrow means the figure goes on forever.

FigurePictureWhat it isHow to name it
PointAn exact spot, drawn as a dotpoint A
LineStraight, goes on forever both ways. No endpointsline AB or line BA
Line segmentPart of a line with 2 endpointsline segment AB or BA
Ray1 endpoint, goes on forever one wayray AB: the endpoint comes first
AngleTwo rays with the same endpoint, the vertexangle ABC: the vertex goes in the middle
Example

A ray starts at point K and goes through point L. What is its name?

The endpoint is K, so K comes first. The order of the letters on the page does not matter.

Answer: ray KL

Kinds of angles

Compare an angle with a right angle, a square corner like the corner of a sheet of paper. A small square in a corner shows a right angle.

AngleSize
AcuteSmaller than a right angle (less than 90°)
RightExactly a square corner (90°)
ObtuseBigger than a right angle, smaller than a straight angle (between 90° and 180°)
StraightA straight line (180°), the same as 2 right angles

Parallel and perpendicular lines

Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, like train tracks. Perpendicular lines cross at right angles, like the lines of a plus sign. Lines that cross at any angle are intersecting.

Line segments can be parallel or perpendicular too. The top and bottom of the letter Z are parallel, and the two line segments of the letter L are perpendicular.

Classify triangles by their angles

TriangleWhat it must have
Acute triangleAll 3 angles acute
Right triangle1 right angle
Obtuse triangle1 obtuse angle

A triangle can never have 2 right angles or 2 obtuse angles: its sides would not meet.

Classify shapes by sides and angles

Sort shapes by asking: Does it have parallel sides? Perpendicular sides (a right angle)? Any acute or obtuse angles?

ShapePairs of parallel sidesRight angles
Square, rectangle24
Parallelogram that leans20
Trapezoidexactly 10 or 2
Right triangle01
Hexagon with equal sides30 (all 6 are obtuse)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up lines, line segments and raysLook at the ends: 2 arrows = line, 2 dots = line segment, 1 dot and 1 arrow = ray
Naming ray KL as ray LKThe endpoint always comes first
Calling a tilted right angle acuteTurning does not change an angle. Check for a square corner
Saying lines are parallel because they do not cross on the pageCheck that they stay the same distance apart
Calling an obtuse triangle acute because 2 angles are acuteName a triangle by its largest angle

faq.q: What is the difference between a line, a line segment and a ray?
faq.a: A line goes on forever in both directions, a line segment has 2 endpoints, and a ray has 1 endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.

faq.q: How do you name a ray?
faq.a: Write the endpoint first, then another point on the ray. A ray that starts at A and goes through B is ray AB; ray BA would start at B.

faq.q: What is the difference between parallel and perpendicular lines?
faq.a: Parallel lines never meet and stay the same distance apart. Perpendicular lines cross and make 4 right angles.

faq.q: How do you classify triangles by their angles?
faq.a: Look at the largest angle. A right triangle has a right angle, an obtuse triangle has an obtuse angle, and an acute triangle has 3 acute angles.

sets.title: Points, lines, line segments and rays

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It has arrows on both ends, so it goes on forever both ways. A line is straight and goes on forever in both directions. The arrows on both ends show this.

items.q: How many endpoints does a line have?
items.e: A line goes on forever in both directions, so it has no endpoints. The points named on a line are not endpoints.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: The endpoint is L, on the right, and the ray goes left through K. Name a ray with its endpoint first, even if you read the letters the other way: ray LK.

items.q: Which figure is most like the edge of a ruler?
items.e: The edge is straight and stops at both ends. It has 2 endpoints, so it is like a line segment.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It has 2 endpoints and no arrows. Standing up does not change what it is. A line segment is part of a line. It has 2 endpoints, so it does not go on forever.

items.q: Which picture shows ray PQ?
items.e: Picture C shows a ray that starts at endpoint P and goes on forever through Q. One picture is ray QP (it starts at Q), one is a line and one is a line segment.

items.q: Which name is correct for this figure?
items.e: Arrows on both ends make it a line. A line can be named with its 2 points in either order: TU or UT.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It stops at 2 endpoints and has no arrows. A line segment is part of a line. It has 2 endpoints, so it does not go on forever.

items.q: Which picture shows line segment MN?
items.e: Picture D has 2 endpoints, M and N, and no arrows. The others go on forever: a line and two rays.

items.q: Are ray AB and ray BA the same ray?
c: No, they start at different points
Yes, they use the same 2 points
items.e: Ray AB starts at A and goes through B. Ray BA starts at B and goes through A, the other way. Only lines and line segments can be named in either order.

items.q: How many endpoints does a ray have?
items.e: A ray has 1 endpoint where it starts. At the other end it goes on forever, so there is no second endpoint.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: There is only a dot with a letter, and no length. A point is an exact spot. It is drawn as a dot and named with one capital letter.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It has one endpoint, G, and one arrow. A ray can point in any direction. A ray has 1 endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. The arrow shows the direction.

items.q: A flashlight beam starts at the flashlight and goes straight out in one direction. Which figure is it most like?
items.e: It has a starting point (the flashlight) and goes on in one direction, like a ray.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: Two rays start at the same point, the vertex. An angle is two rays that share the same endpoint, called the vertex.

items.q: Which name is correct for this figure?
items.e: It has 2 endpoints and no arrows, so it is a line segment. You can name it with its endpoints in either order: CD or DC.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: The endpoint is Y at the bottom, and the arrow goes up through X. The endpoint comes first: ray YX.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It has arrows on both ends. Tilting a line does not change what it is. A line is straight and goes on forever in both directions. The arrows on both ends show this.

items.q: What is this figure called?
items.e: It starts at one endpoint and has one arrow. A ray has 1 endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. The arrow shows the direction.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint and one arrow, so it is a ray. Name a ray with its endpoint first: P, then Q. Ray QP would start at Q.

sets.title: Acute, right, obtuse and straight angles

items.q: Lena opens her laptop. The screen leans back past a square corner, but it is not flat. What kind of angle do the screen and the keyboard make?
items.e: The angle is wider than a right angle (a square corner) but less than a straight angle (flat), so it is obtuse.
The opening is wider than a square corner but not a straight line, so it is an obtuse angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90 degrees).

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The opening is smaller than a square corner, so it is an acute angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The opening is smaller than a square corner, so it is an acute angle.

items.q: A clock shows 6:00. What kind of angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make?
items.e: At 6:00 one hand points straight up and the other straight down. Together they make a straight line: 180 degrees.

items.q: How many right angles make one straight angle?
items.e: A right angle is 90 degrees and a straight angle is 180 degrees. 90 + 90 = 180, so 2 right angles make a straight angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90 degrees). Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: A clock shows 4:00. What kind of angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make?
items.e: At 4:00 the hands are 4 hour marks apart: 4 × 30 = 120 degrees. That is more than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

items.q: A clock shows 2:00. What kind of angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make?
items.e: At 2:00 the hands are 2 hour marks apart. Each hour mark is 30 degrees, so the angle is 60 degrees, smaller than a right angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The opening is smaller than a square corner, so it is an acute angle.

items.q: What is a name for this angle?
items.e: The vertex is B, where the two rays meet. The vertex letter always goes in the middle: angle ABC (or angle CBA).
The two rays point in opposite directions and make a straight line. That is a straight angle (180 degrees), the size of 2 right angles.
Picture B shows an angle wider than a right angle but less than a straight line. The straight line is a straight angle, not an obtuse angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle (90 degrees). Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: A clock shows 3:00. What kind of angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make?
items.e: At 3:00 the hands make a square corner: a quarter turn, 90 degrees.
The opening is wider than a square corner but not a straight line, so it is an obtuse angle.

items.q: Which point is the vertex of angle RST?
items.e: In an angle's name, the middle letter is the vertex. In angle RST, the middle letter is S.
Picture C shows an angle smaller than a square corner. The others are a right angle and two obtuse angles.

items.q: Sam says this angle is acute because it is tilted. Is he right?
c: No, it is a right angle
items.e: The small square shows a square corner, so it is a right angle. Turning an angle does not change its size.

items.q: Which letter has parallel line segments but no perpendicular line segments?
items.e: Z has a top and a bottom that are parallel, and its slanted middle is not at a right angle to them.

items.q: What is the best word for these two lines?
items.e: The lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, so they are parallel. The arrows show they are lines, not line segments.

items.q: What is the best word for these two lines?
items.e: The lines cross and make right angles (see the small square), so they are perpendicular. They also intersect, but perpendicular is the best word because it tells more.

items.q: Which letter has both parallel and perpendicular line segments?
items.e: F has 2 parallel line segments going across, and both are perpendicular to the line segment going down.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to line AB?
items.e: Line EF crosses line AB at a right angle (see the small square). Line CD is parallel to line AB, and line AE is just another name for line AB, because A and E are both on it.

items.q: Which street is perpendicular to Elm St?
items.e: Main St crosses Elm St at a right angle (a square corner). Lake Rd crosses it too, but at a slant. Oak St is parallel to Elm St.

items.q: What is the best word for these two lines?
items.e: The lines tilt the same way and stay the same distance apart. They will never meet, so they are parallel.

items.q: Perpendicular lines meet to make what kind of angles?
items.e: Perpendicular lines cross at a square corner, so they make right angles.

items.q: Two lines cross, and one of the angles they make is a right angle. How many right angles do they make in all?
items.e: When two lines cross they make 4 angles. If one is a right angle, all 4 are right angles: the lines are perpendicular.

items.q: What is the best word for these two lines?
items.e: They do not cross on the page, but they get closer and closer. If you keep going to the right, they will meet. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart.

items.q: The two rails of a straight train track never meet. Which word describes them?
items.e: The rails stay the same distance apart and never meet, like parallel lines.

items.q: Which street is parallel to Oak St?
items.e: Oak St and Elm St both go straight across and stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel. Main St and Lake Rd cross Oak St.

items.q: Which letter has no parallel and no perpendicular line segments?
items.e: V has 2 slanted line segments that meet but not at a right angle, and they are not parallel.

items.q: What is the best word for these two lines?
items.e: The lines cross, but not at a right angle. They are intersecting, not perpendicular.

items.q: Tom says these two lines are parallel because they do not cross. Is he right?
items.e: The gap between the lines gets smaller to the right, so the lines would meet if we drew more of them. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart everywhere.

items.q: Which letter has perpendicular line segments but no parallel line segments?
items.e: L has 2 line segments that meet at a right angle, and nothing parallel.

items.q: Main St and Lake Rd do not cross on this map. Are they parallel?
c: Yes, they do not cross here
items.e: Main St goes straight up and down, but Lake Rd slants. If both streets kept going down past the map, they would meet.

items.q: Which line is parallel to line CD?
items.e: Line AB and line CD go the same way and never meet, so they are parallel. Line EF is perpendicular to both, and line CF is the same line as line CD.

items.q: Can two parallel lines ever cross?
items.e: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart forever, so they never cross, no matter how far they go.

items.q: Lake Rd crosses Oak St. Are these two streets perpendicular?
items.e: Lake Rd crosses at a slant, so the angles are not right angles. Crossing is not enough: perpendicular lines must meet at right angles.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: The sides do not meet at the bottom left, so the shape is not closed. A triangle is a closed shape with 3 sides.

items.q: Can a triangle have 2 obtuse angles?
c: No, the sides would not meet
Yes, if it is very big
items.e: Two obtuse angles would make the 2 sides spread apart, so they could never meet to close the triangle.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 110°, 40° and 30°. Two of its angles are acute. What kind of triangle is it?
items.e: 110° is more than 90°, so it is obtuse. A triangle is named by its largest angle. Every triangle has at least 2 acute angles, so that does not make it acute.

items.q: Every triangle has at least how many acute angles?
items.e: A triangle can have at most 1 right angle or 1 obtuse angle. So at least 2 of its 3 angles are always acute.

items.q: How many acute angles does this triangle have?
items.e: One angle is a right angle (the square). The other 2 angles are smaller, so they are acute.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is an acute triangle.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is an obtuse triangle. The other 2 angles are acute.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: One angle is wider than a right angle, so it is an obtuse triangle. The other 2 angles are acute.

items.q: Can a triangle have 2 right angles?
c: Yes, if it is very big
No, the sides would not meet
items.e: If 2 angles were right angles, the 2 sides going up from them would be parallel and never meet. So the shape could not close.

items.q: A triangle has angles of 90°, 30° and 60°. What kind of triangle is it?
items.e: It has a 90° angle, which is a right angle, so it is a right triangle.

items.q: Ana says this is an acute triangle because 2 of its angles are acute. Is she right?
c: Yes, it is a wide triangle
No, it is a right triangle
No, it has an obtuse angle
items.e: The top angle is wider than a right angle, so it is an obtuse triangle. Every triangle has at least 2 acute angles, so look at the largest angle.

items.q: Which is a right triangle?
items.e: Picture D has a right angle (the small square). The others have no right angle.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is an acute triangle.

items.q: A ramp leans against a wall. The wall stands straight up from the flat ground. The ground, the wall and the ramp make a triangle. What kind of triangle is it?
items.e: The wall meets the ground at a square corner, a right angle. A triangle with a right angle is a right triangle.

items.q: Which is an obtuse triangle?
items.e: Picture C has one angle wider than a right angle. The others are a right triangle and two acute triangles.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: The small square shows one right angle, so it is a right triangle. The other 2 angles are acute. Turning a triangle does not change its angles.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: Count the sides: there are 4, because the top corner is cut off. A triangle has exactly 3 sides.

items.q: How many obtuse angles does this triangle have?
items.e: Only the angle where the bottom side meets the left side is wider than a right angle. A triangle can never have more than 1 obtuse angle.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: The small square shows one right angle, so it is a right triangle. The other 2 angles are acute.

items.q: What kind of triangle is this?
items.e: All 3 angles are smaller than a right angle, so it is an acute triangle.

sets.title: Classify shapes by sides and angles

items.q: A door is a rectangle. How many pairs of parallel sides does it have?
items.e: The top and bottom are parallel, and the 2 sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs (4 is the number of sides).

items.q: A window has 4 right angles. Mia says it has no perpendicular sides because none of its sides cross. Is she right?
c: No, its sides meet at right angles
Yes, the sides do not cross
items.e: Two sides are perpendicular when they meet at a right angle. They do not have to cross. Every corner of the window joins 2 perpendicular sides.

items.q: Which shape has no right angles?
items.e: Picture C has no square corners. The others each have at least one right angle (see the small squares).

items.q: Which shape always has perpendicular sides?
items.e: A right triangle always has a right angle, so 2 of its sides are perpendicular. A rhombus or a trapezoid has right angles only sometimes, and an obtuse triangle never does.

items.q: Which shape has perpendicular sides but no parallel sides?
items.e: Picture A is a right triangle: 2 sides meet at a right angle, and no sides are parallel. The rectangle and both trapezoids have parallel sides.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this shape have?
items.e: This hexagon has 6 sides, and each side is parallel to the side across from it. 6 sides make 3 pairs.

items.q: Which shape has no parallel sides?
items.e: Picture B is a pentagon with 5 equal sides. None of its sides go the same way. The hexagon has 3 pairs of parallel sides, the trapezoid 1 pair and the rectangle 2 pairs.

items.q: Which shape always has 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 right angles?
items.e: Every rectangle has 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides. A parallelogram or a rhombus has right angles only sometimes, and a trapezoid has only 1 pair of parallel sides.

items.q: Kai says every shape with a right angle also has parallel sides. Which shape shows that he is wrong?
items.e: A right triangle has a right angle but no parallel sides. The rectangle, the square and the right trapezoid all have parallel sides.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: There are right angles at the 2 bottom corners and at the top point (see the small squares). The 2 angles where the roof meets the walls are obtuse.

items.q: Which shape can never have parallel sides?
items.e: Any 2 sides of a triangle meet at a corner, so no 2 sides can be parallel.

items.q: Which shape has an obtuse angle?
items.e: Picture A is a hexagon. All 6 of its angles are wider than a right angle. The square has right angles only, and the triangles have acute angles and a right angle.

items.q: A garden bed has 4 sides. Only the front edge and the back edge are parallel, and none of its corners are right angles. What shape is it?
items.e: 4 sides with exactly 1 pair of parallel sides make a trapezoid. A parallelogram or a rectangle has 2 pairs.

items.q: A yield sign is a triangle with 3 equal sides. Each angle is 60°. What kind of triangle is it?
items.e: 60° is less than 90°, so all 3 angles are acute. That makes it an acute triangle.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The small squares show 2 right angles, both on the left side. The other 2 angles are acute and obtuse.

items.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Picture D is a trapezoid: only its top and bottom are parallel. The parallelogram and rectangle have 2 pairs, and the triangle has none.

items.q: Which shape has 2 pairs of parallel sides but no right angles?
items.e: Picture B is a parallelogram that leans, so it has no right angles. The square has right angles, the trapezoid has only 1 pair of parallel sides, and the kite has none.

items.q: A shape has 4 sides, 2 pairs of parallel sides and no right angles. All 4 sides are the same length. What is it?
items.e: 4 equal sides make a rhombus. With no right angles it is not a square, and with 2 pairs of parallel sides it is not a trapezoid.

items.q: How many obtuse angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 top angles are wider than a right angle, so they are obtuse. The 2 bottom angles are acute.

items.q: Luis cuts a square piece of bread from one corner to the opposite corner. What kind of triangles are the 2 pieces?
items.e: Each piece keeps one corner of the square, which is a right angle. So both pieces are right triangles.
